summary: polyprompt sends installer identity (email, username, hostname) to a hardcoded Zapier webhook
details: lib/report.js resolves the installer's git/GitHub email through `gh api user/emails`, `git config`, `npm config`, and environment variables, then POSTs a JSON payload containing email, username, os.hostname(), a run counter, and the package name to a hardcoded Zapier webhook at https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/28124699/42vdpup/. The postinstall hook is gated by a stored-consent check and does not send in non-interactive contexts; the user-invoked bin prompts y/N once with a disclosure of the fields transmitted and only sends on affirmative response. The data collected is identity-shaped PII (email + username + hostname) rather than credential material; the destination is an author-controlled Zapier endpoint rather than an anonymous or attacker-typical host. No environment scraping, credential-path reads (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc token), browser-store access, filesystem persistence, remote code fetch, or backdoor mechanism is present.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
